section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the Alter Rebbe's Tanya and his son's gloss explaining that the perfection of the Messianic era and resurrection depends on our actions and service, with "our actions" referring to the Messianic era and "our service" to the resurrection.
section.t: And this will be understood by prefacing what is stated in Tanya,
that the ultimate perfection of the days of Mashiach and the resurrection of the dead depends on our actions and our service throughout the duration of the exile,
and my master, my father, the Baal HaHilula wrote in his glosses on the margin of his copy of the Tanya
(which for several years was in captivity, and in the last period it was redeemed,
(his copy of the Tanya together with other books of his)
from captivity and arrived here),
that the matter of the two expressions,
"our actions" and "our service,"
will be understood from what is stated later in Igeret HaKodesh, Epistle 12, beginning with the phrase "And the act of charity etc.," see there.
And afterwards he continues,
that it can be said,
that "our actions" refers to the days of Mashiach, and "our service" refers to the resurrection of the dead.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Baal HaHilula's reference to Igeret HaKodesh clarifies the distinction between "action" (habitual, natural) and "service" (with great effort against one's nature), and that this distinction applies to the terms "our actions" and "our service" in Tanya.
section.t: And behold, the intention of the Baal HaHilula in what he references to Igeret HaKodesh, Epistle 12, beginning with the phrase "And the act of charity etc.," is apparently to what is explained in Igeret HaKodesh there,
the difference between "action" and "service,"
"for the term 'action' applies to something that has already been done, or that is done automatically constantly, and it is a thing that is ongoing and regular always, etc.,
(in contrast,)

the term 'service' applies only to something that a person does with immense effort against the nature of his soul, only that he nullifies his nature and his will before the will of the Supreme One, blessed be He."
From this it is understood,
that so too is the interpretation of the two expressions "our actions" and "our service" in the Tanya here,
that "our actions" refers to the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos according to nature and habit,
and "our service" refers to exertion in Torah and mitzvos beyond nature and habit.
But,
from the fact that he writes that the two expressions
("our actions" and "our service")
will be understood from what is stated in Igeret HaKodesh, Epistle 12,
and he concludes
(after referencing the aforementioned Igeret HaKodesh)
"see there,"
it implies that his intention in what he references to the aforementioned Igeret HaKodesh is
(in addition to the difference between "action" and "service" in general)
also to what is explained there regarding the matter of the act of charity,
that through contemplation of this
("see there")
the distinction between "our actions" and "our service" will be understood in greater depth,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the distinction between "our actions" and "our service" is that "our actions" includes even effort to reveal the natural G-dly soul trait, while "our service" is effort that surpasses even that natural G-dly soul trait.
section.t: For behold, it is explained in Igeret HaKodesh there regarding the matter of the act of charity, that this "that Israel by their nature are merciful
and performers of kindnesses
(it is)
because their souls are drawn from His attributes, blessed be He, in which kindness prevails over the attribute of judgment, etc., therefore the soul is called 'the daughter of a kohen'"
(a kohen being a man of kindness).
And he explains there,
that "the charity that is drawn from this aspect is called by the name 'the act of charity,' for the term 'action' applies to a thing that is ongoing and regular always,
(because)
the attribute of kindness and mercy was implanted in the souls of all the house of Israel from the time of their creation
and their descent from His attributes, blessed be He."
And this means,
that even though the nature of kindness within him is
(not from his animal soul,
but rather)
from his G-dly soul,
nevertheless,
the charity that he performs because of this nature,
is called by the name "the act of charity."
And the "service of charity" is when his giving of charity is beyond even the nature of his G-dly soul.
And from this it is understood,
that the distinction between "our actions" and "our service"
(in the entirety of Torah and mitzvos)
is,
that even when his animal soul conceals the nature of the G-dly soul,
and he needs to exert himself to remove the covering and concealment of the animal soul and to reveal the nature of the G-dly soul,
nevertheless, it is included in "our actions,"
since his exertion is only to reveal the nature of his G-dly soul,
and "our service" is when his exertion is beyond even the nature of his G-dly soul.
